customManagers.description: mise's own version in the workflows (setup-mise takes it as an input), annotated with a '# renovate:' comment

packageRules.description: The tools the sign-image workflow runs beside the signing identity (.mise.sign.toml) are locked in mise.sign.lock, which scripts/check-mise-locks holds to what a real `mise lock` writes. Renovate can't write that lock (it needs a mise.lock beside the config and a global allowedUnsafeExecutions that the hosted app doesn't give us), so a bump of the pin alone fails validate. These bumps wait for approval on the Dependency Dashboard (they stay visible there, so a stale cosign shows), never automerge, and carry the procedure in the PR body
prBodyNotes: **This PR is not mergeable as it stands:** `mise.sign.lock` must change with the pin, or `scripts/check-mise-locks` fails `validate`. Renovate does not write it. On this branch, run `MISE_ENV=sign mise lock --platform linux-x64,macos-arm64 <tool>` for each tool bumped (`GITHUB_TOKEN` set, to avoid API rate limits), read the diff (a new `url` or `checksum` host, a lost `provenance` line, or a changed platform set is a red flag; do not edit `scripts/check-mise-locks` to make it pass), run `mise exec -- scripts/validate`, and push the lock commit signed. Renovate stops rebasing a branch someone else committed to. After merge, a release of this repo is needed before callers' Renovate sees the bump (README, "Releases and how callers pick them up").

packageRules.description: jq is pinned in both mise files and must be equal (a comment in each says so): one PR, and under the sign-tools approval rule above because one of the two is locked

mise itself is installed by the validate job and by sign-image.yaml (which holds id-token): one PR for both files, read the release notes. mise releases almost daily, so one weekly batch (Mondays before 5am; security-fix PRs ignore the schedule)
Skip a brand-new major's X.0.0 until X.0.1 or X.1.0 exists (Renovate can't see 'has a patch' directly)
Major bumps need a human to read the changelog, and a longer wait than the 3-day default
